Bred specimens of this beautiful large tetra – the real one, with bright yellow ventral fins – are now available. Currently the fish are 7-9 cm long.

These tetras grow up to 20-25 cm long.
The fish need really spacious tanks to grow to a good size.

They love a strong current. Here they stand – preferably under a piece of driftwood or so – near the water surface and wait for prey.

Chalceus are excellent jumpers, so the tank must always be perfectly covered.
The members of the genus Chalceus can be best compared with native species of trout. Like these, Chalceus prefer to feed on insects etc. that fall on the water surface.

One should keep them in groups, best 10 specimens or more, because otherwise the fish can be quarrelsome against conspecifics.

Against other tankmates Chalceus are absolutely peaceful. Plants are ignored.
